claim: No general-audience account has set the Budzyn et al. colonoscopy deskilling result (Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology 2025, adenoma detection falling from 28.4% to 22.4% in non-AI colonoscopies after AI adoption) beside the experimental studies of generative AI and reasoning or essay writing, while also reporting the colonoscopy study's own stated limitations.
counterexample: The PulmCCM newsletter piece 'The New Era of AI De-Skilling is Here' (September 5, 2025) places the Budzyn colonoscopy result directly beside the Kosmyna et al. 'Your Brain on ChatGPT' essay-writing study and the Microsoft/Swiss business-school critical-thinking studies in a single general-audience account. It satisfies two of the three conjunctive conditions. Whether it also reports the colonoscopy study's own stated limitations (observational design, sensitivity to selection bias and confounding — per the paper itself at Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 10:896-903) cannot be confirmed from publicly visible snippets because the full article is subscriber-gated. The ACG EBGI summary (gi.org, September 2025) similarly cites both Budzyn and the Kosmyna essay-writing preprint in the same document, but is a specialist journal summary rather than a clearly general-audience piece. The claim therefore survives only in the narrow form: no confirmed single general-audience account has done all three things simultaneously — the two-out-of-three case (Budzyn + essay-writing AI studies) is clearly broken.
citation: https://www.pulmccm.org/p/the-new-era-of-ai-de-skilling-is (PulmCCM, September 5, 2025); https://gi.org/journals-publications/ebgi/zhou_sep2025/ (ACG EBGI, September 2025); colonoscopy study limitation source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2468125325001335 (Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 10:896-903, 2025)
quote: "Writing an essay using one's own brain produces a distinctly different neurologic activation pattern compared to using ChatGPT, and results in deeper understanding." (PulmCCM, same article that covers Budzyn)
why_it_still_matters: This changes the sentence materially but not the piece's conclusion. The two-out-of-three version of the claim — that no general-audience account has placed the colonoscopy deskilling result beside the generative-AI-and-writing/reasoning literature — is clearly broken by PulmCCM and the ACG EBGI summary. The third prong (reporting the colonoscopy study's own stated limitations) is unconfirmed due to paywalling of the full PulmCCM text, so the sentence survives only in that narrower, harder-to-verify form. Any piece relying on the claim as written should either verify the PulmCCM full text or restate the claim as 'no account has done all three simultaneously with the limitations explicitly named.'
inherited_from: The claim appears to be original to the piece being assessed, not inherited from a guideline or prior review. However, the colonoscopy study's own stated limitation language — 'Despite the observational design of our study, with its sensitivity to selection bias and confounding' — is from the paper itself (Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 10:896-903, 2025, ScienceDirect abstract). The claim's third prong is therefore testable against that specific language.
